definitions.explanation: Describes a person who tends to argue using logic and reasoning in an excessive or annoying way. Carries a negative connotation — implying the person is difficult to deal with because they always insist on logical explanations.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{理屈|りくつ}っぽいから{話|はなし}しにくい。
examples.english: He's so argumentative that he's hard to talk to.

examples.japanese: あまり{理屈|りくつ}っぽいことを{言|い}わないで。
examples.english: Don't be so pedantic about it.

examples.japanese: {理屈|りくつ}っぽい{性格|せいかく}のせいで、{友達|ともだち}が{少|すく}ないと{自分|じぶん}でも{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think my argumentative personality is why I don't have many friends.

notes:
FORMS:
Uses the ～っぽい suffix meaning "tending toward" or "-ish": {怒|おこ}りっぽい (short-tempered), {忘|わす}れっぽい (forgetful), {飽|あ}きっぽい (easily bored). The suffix generally carries a mildly negative nuance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {理屈|りくつ}っぽい{人|ひと} (a pedantic person)
- {理屈|りくつ}っぽい{性格|せいかく} (an argumentative personality)
- {理屈|りくつ}っぽいことを{言|い}う (to say pedantic things)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {屁理屈|へりくつ}を{言|い}う: to make specious arguments — more negative, implies bad-faith reasoning
- くどい: long-winded — focuses on repetitive explanation rather than logic
- {論理的|ろんりてき}: logical — neutral/positive, unlike {理屈|りくつ}っぽい which is negative
